A few notes on how this is built for MailChimp:

- **Table-based layout** — email clients (especially Outlook) don't support flexbox/grid, so the 2-column card grid and structure use nested `<table>`s, which is the standard for reliable rendering across inboxes.
- **All styles inline** — MailChimp's editor sometimes strips `<style>` blocks on paste; only the responsive stacking rule (mobile) lives in `<head>`, everything else is inline so it survives untouched.
- **Font fallback** — custom fonts like Archivo Black usually won't load in email clients, so I used `Arial Black` with `font-weight:900` as the closest safe substitute for that bold, condensed look.
- **Gradient caveat** — the banner gradient is CSS `linear-gradient`, which most modern clients (Gmail, Apple Mail, Outlook.com, mobile) render fine, but classic desktop Outlook (Windows, using Word's rendering engine) will fall back to the solid `#3E7DAD` I set as a backup color instead of showing the gradient. If your audience is heavy on desktop Outlook, let me know and I can add a VML fallback for a true gradient there.
- **Aug 31–Sept 4 card** — since it spans two months, I split the label to "AUG–SEPT" over "31–4" to keep it inside the small card header without crowding.
